assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly consequential body of evidence and analysis explaining how trade and technology reshape local labour markets, employment and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson form a coherent core for the stated contribution; the evidence base is especially closely associated with their work.
assessment.maturity: The findings have endured extensive empirical scrutiny and have substantially shaped labour-economics research and policy debate.
uncertainties: The relative importance of trade, technology and other concurrent forces remains an active empirical question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern treatment of monopsony has transformed understanding of wage setting and labour-market power, with broad practical relevance.
assessment.attribution: Manning is the clearest single attribution for the unified modern monopsony framework in the listed contribution.
assessment.maturity: The framework is longstanding and now supported by a large empirical literature on employer concentration, wages and mobility.
uncertainties: The appropriate division of credit between theoretical formulation and later empirical measurement is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative-data measurement of mobility has made inequality of opportunity more precisely measurable and policy-relevant.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are central to the linked research program and its place-based mobility evidence.
assessment.maturity: The approach has generated a durable research infrastructure and a broad follow-on literature.
uncertainties: Measurement of mobility does not by itself establish the causal mechanisms behind geographic differences.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correspondence-study evidence supplied unusually direct and influential evidence on discrimination in hiring.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are a particularly identifiable pair for the landmark audit-study contribution.
assessment.maturity: The methods and central findings have been replicated and extended across settings over many years.
uncertainties: Audit studies identify responses to applications, while inference about later workplace treatment and aggregate mechanisms requires care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification established a rigorous way to draw informative conclusions without concealing the consequences of weak assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski is foundational for the program, with Tamer a central contributor to moment-inequality implementation.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are well established and widely used across econometrics and applied work.
uncertainties: The contribution spans a broad intellectual program, making a narrow laureate set difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods became indispensable tools for credible empirical analysis with persistent outcomes and unobserved heterogeneity.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Bond and Blundell have a direct, tightly connected claim to the central estimators and their extension.
assessment.maturity: The methods have had decades of use, refinement and diagnostic evaluation.
uncertainties: Their practical reliability depends on instrument choice and specification, issues that can be consequential in applications.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life conditions and skill formation has altered economic understanding of when inequality originates and which interventions may matter.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond and Cunha represent complementary empirical and conceptual pillars of the stated contribution.
assessment.maturity: The field has accumulated a substantial body of quasi-experimental evidence and long-run follow-up.
uncertainties: Evidence on early-life effects is heterogeneous across contexts, and translating estimates into intervention design remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The integration of theory and empirical measurement of selection in insurance markets has materially improved analysis of health and other insurance markets.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav and Salanie each have central and complementary claims within the listed theory-and-measurement contribution.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is longstanding, highly influential and supported by a broad applied literature.
uncertainties: Selection patterns and welfare implications can vary substantially by institutional setting and contract design.
